title: MLO proteins are essential host factors hijacked by powdery mildew
content: Obligate biotrophic pathogens such as powdery mildew (PM) fungi depend on living host tissues for their development (Schulze-Lefert and Panstruga 2003). Soon after penetrating the host cell wall, PM forms the haustorium, a specialized structure that is separated from the host cell cytoplasm by the host-derived extra-haustorial membrane (EHM). Haustorium and EHM make the interaction interface where effectors and nutrients are translocated between PM and plant cells. This process leads to the biogenesis of an apoplastic environment encased between the fungal plasma membrane and the invaginated host plasma membrane (Berkey et al. 2017). To keep this apoplastic environment encased, a physical barrier called “neckband” is formed to seal the fungal and host plasma membranes in the haustorium neck (Gil and Gay 1977).
